title: AI-Run Modern LaTeX Manuscript Workflow and Replication Packet
description:
Compact workflow and replication record for the Modern LaTeX Editions of Mathematics Manuscripts project. It documents the AI-run scan-to-TeX-to-translation-to-audit-to-publication workflow, including local source acquisition, OCR/math-OCR witness generation, source-image slicing, high-DPI object crops, TeX compilation, web review handoffs, GitHub mirroring, and Zenodo publication.

Latest update. Adds workflow-addendum-20260612-object-level-audit.md, a small public addendum distilled from local diagram/table repair audits. The addendum records that diagram and table promotion should be object-level rather than page-level: a promoted object needs a source object witness, output render witness, stable object ID, and explicit ledger verdict. Full-page screenshots and contact sheets are orientation aids, not authority, and screenshots or crops must not silently replace reconstructed TeX.

Workflow status. The record is a reusable workflow packet, not a claim that any particular mathematical edition is critically complete. OCR, VLM, detector, crop, and candidate-TeX outputs are witness and locator layers unless a source-specific audit promotes them. Source scans and source-object witnesses remain authority for transcription claims.

Corrections and contributions. Workflow corrections, tool notes, reproducibility improvements, and issue reports can be suggested through the GitHub mirror via issues or pull requests: https://github.com/KokunoYumeto/modern-latex-manuscripts.
notes: Adds workflow-addendum-20260612-object-level-audit.md. This addendum distills local diagram/table audit lessons: promotion of diagrams, tables, determinant displays, and dense formula objects should require a stable object ID, source object witness, output render witness, and explicit ledger verdict. Contact sheets and screenshots are triage/orientation aids, not authority; image-backed objects must be labelled rather than silently treated as reconstructed TeX.
